tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: ZEFF AI is a multi-surface AI workspace spanning Next.js web, Electron desktop, and Capacitor Android. Start with README.md for how to run the app locally, then read package.json to see the unified toolchain: Next.js, Prisma, Electron packaging, RAG indexing, and evaluation scripts that glue the monorepo together.

tour.title: Root Layout Entry
tour.description: The App Router boots from src/app/layout.tsx, which sets metadata, viewport, theme, and global providers for every route. RootSessionProvider injects NextAuth session context at the top of the tree, while ThemeProvider applies and persists light/dark theme so landing, auth, and workspace pages share one chrome.
tour.languageLesson: In the Next.js App Router, root layout.tsx is a Server Component that wraps all pages; client providers like session and theme must be nested inside client wrappers so the server layout can still stream HTML.

tour.title: Authentication Flow
tour.description: Building on the session provider from Step 2, src/auth.ts configures NextAuth providers, callbacks, and sign-in handlers. The catch-all /api/auth/[...nextauth] route exposes those handlers over HTTP, while login/signup pages collect credentials and apiAuth.ts centralizes requireSession/requireUserId checks used by nearly every protected API.

tour.title: Chat Workspace UI
tour.description: After sign-in, users land in the authenticated /app segment. app/layout.tsx wraps workspace routes with shared chrome, app/page.tsx mounts the main experience, and ChatWorkspace orchestrates messages, streaming, tools, and side panels while Sidebar navigates between chat, library, and workspace tools.

tour.title: Chat API & Agents
tour.description: ChatWorkspace talks to /api/chat, the highest fan-out API route in the graph. That handler delegates to agentRoute for streaming tool turns and toolGeneration for structured outputs like math annotations and practice sets—the core AI runtime behind the UI from Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js route handlers export named HTTP functions (e.g. POST). Streaming agent responses typically return a ReadableStream so the client can render tokens incrementally instead of waiting for a full JSON body.

tour.title: Domain Libraries
tour.description: Shared TypeScript libraries sit under the chat UI and APIs. workspace.ts owns membership, invites, and role checks used by workspace APIs; plans.ts defines plan IDs and pricing helpers consumed by checkout and admin; together they form the domain vocabulary the product routes depend on.

tour.title: Billing & Checkout
tour.description: Monetization builds on plans from Step 6. The /checkout page starts a purchase, /api/checkout creates and confirms orders, billing.ts fulfills paid orders and validates ownership, and /api/billing/orders lists a user's order history—keeping payment fulfillment out of the chat path.

tour.title: Admin & Security
tour.description: Admin surfaces sit behind requireAdmin, which enforces session (and optional MFA) before any /admin page or security API runs. The admin layout and security dashboard client then expose self-scans, findings by domain, and severity stats—the operational control plane layered on the same auth primitives from Step 3.

tour.title: Electron Desktop
tour.description: The desktop app wraps the same Next.js UI in Electron. main.js creates the window, enforces navigation allowlists, and wires backup IPC; preload.js exposes a narrow zeffBackup API through contextBridge so the renderer never gets raw Node access.
tour.languageLesson: Electron's contextBridge is the safe way to expose IPC: define explicit methods in preload instead of enabling nodeIntegration, which would let renderer code reach the filesystem directly.

tour.title: Android Mobile Shell
tour.description: Mobile uses Capacitor as a thin native shell around the web app. MainActivity extends BridgeActivity with no custom native logic, AndroidManifest declares permissions and the launcher activity, and android/README.md documents web-asset sync, Android Studio setup, and release APK/AAB builds.

tour.title: Data & Prisma
tour.description: Persistence underpins every authenticated flow from Steps 3–8. schema.prisma defines Auth.js models and ZEFF domain tables on PostgreSQL, prisma.ts is the high fan-in client singleton imported across APIs, and prisma.config.ts wires datasource options for tooling and migrations.
tour.languageLesson: Prisma models map 1:1 to database tables; a shared PrismaClient singleton (often cached on globalThis in Next.js) avoids exhausting connection pools during hot reload.

tour.title: Docs & Deployment
tour.description: Close the tour with how the system ships and is operated. vercel.json schedules the dormant-account cron, db-push.yml applies Prisma schema changes on main, and build-windows-installer.yml produces the Electron Windows artifact—connecting web deploy, database, and desktop release pipelines.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows declare on triggers, jobs, and steps. Separating db-push from installer builds keeps schema deploys independent of desktop packaging.
